rulers.name: Sam Nujoma
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: 'The country officially became independent on 21 March 1990. Sam Nujoma was sworn in as the first President of Namibia'; his '15-year rule' ended in 2005.

rulers.name: Hifikepunye Pohamba
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: The page: succeeded Nujoma in 2005 and 'served the maximum two terms'; it gives Geingob's election in December 2014 but no inauguration date, so 2015 is the researcher's reading of the handover year.

rulers.name: Hage Geingob
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: Won the presidency in December 2014, re-elected December 2019, died 4 February 2024.

rulers.name: Nangolo Mbumba
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: Succeeded Geingob on 4 February 2024; his term ended in March 2025 (after Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah's election), beyond the 2024 end of this dossier.

keyframe_review.note: 832,435 km2 against the infobox 825,615 km2 (ratio 1.008, fine). Cliopatria's outline already contains the four Walvis Bay cells (checked with the gazetteer: the 25 km disc around Walvis Bay is wholly inside the 1990 shape), but 'In 1990, South West Africa gained independence as Namibia, but Walvis Bay remained under South African sovereignty' until 1 March 1994. The correction holds for 1990-1993; from 1994 see namibia_1994. The South Africa dossier makes the matching correction.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the unchanged Cliopatria shape from 1994, so that the 1990-1993 correction does not run on. No border change is recorded on either page after 1994.
Identical to the 1990 shape; the Namibia page records no change in 2024 and gives only unspecified 'disputes regarding borders and construction plans'.

region.text: South West Africa, now Namibia, without Walvis Bay

ledger.note: 1990: Namibia becomes independent from South Africa. Infobox 'Independence: 21 March 1990, from South Africa'; 'The country officially became independent on 21 March 1990. Sam Nujoma was sworn in as the first President of Namibia at a ceremony attended by Nelson Mandela of South Africa' (Namibia page); Walvis Bay 'remained under South African sovereignty' (Walvis Bay page).

region.text: Walvis Bay and the Penguin Islands, 'a confirmed area of 1,124 square kilometres'

ledger.note: 1994: Walvis Bay returns to Namibia on 1 March. 'South Africa formally transferred sovereignty of Walvis Bay and the Penguin Islands to Namibia on 1 March 1994' (Walvis Bay page; a Joint Administrative Authority had run the enclave since the 1992 agreement; the Namibia page says only 'in 1994').

wars.name: Second Congo War
wars.outcome: No territorial result for Namibia: 'In 1998, Namibia Defence Force troops were sent to the Democratic Republic of the Congo' as part of a SADC contingent.
wars.note: The Namibia page gives the deployment year only and does not name the war. End year 2003 added by the reviewer from the Second Congo War page (infobox '2 August 1998 - 18 July 2003'; Namibia among the 'Pro-government' belligerents, with deployments in 1999 and 2000-2001).

wars.name: Caprivi Strip secessionist attempt
wars.outcome: The government 'quashed a secessionist attempt in the northeastern Caprivi Strip' in 1999; the rebels (Caprivi Liberation Army, led by Mishake Muyongo) held no ground the page records, so no contested zone is drawn.
wars.note: Page gives the year and the aim of the CLA; no battle dates.

certainty.note: Walvis Bay's boundary is the 1911 settlement ('a confirmed area of 1,124 square kilometres'), the rest are colonial-era treaty and survey lines; the Namibia page says Namibia 'has been involved in various disputes regarding borders' without detail, so none is drawn as contested.

notes: Page budget 1-2: both pages opened. (1) Cliopatria's Namibia shape includes Walvis Bay from 1990; the enclave stayed South African until 1 March 1994, so namibia_1990 is adjusted for 1990-1993 and a new keyframe namibia_1994 restores the full shape; the South Africa dossier carries the mirror image. (2) South Africa's own dossier dates the independence loss to 1990-03 and cites the South-West Africa page; this dossier cites the Namibia page. (3) The South African Border War (the war of independence) is not given dates by the Namibia page and predates the state; it is left to the South Africa dossier. (4) The Kasikili/Sedudu island case with Botswana, the Orange River question with South Africa and any Angolan frontier matter are not on the Namibia page and were not opened, so no contest is recorded. (5) Rulers: Pohamba and Geingob handover year 2015 is the researcher's reading (the page gives the December 2014 election). (6) No gazetteer names are missing.
